added_claim_errors: Ties the no-penalty delay to the 400 employees ('well over Medicare's 20-employee threshold... it lets you delay Part B'). Under 20 employees, says 'you'd need to enroll'. This is imprecise: the SEP doesn't depend on employer size; size only decides which plan pays first (minor, per key).
'you might need a Part D plan, and possibly Part B to get it': imprecise. Part D needs Part A or Part B, so someone who has premium-free Part A doesn't need Part B for it (hedged, minor).
'(some do; most don't)' on plans requiring Medicare at 65: an unsourced generalization, though plausible.

'When your coworker would be right: ... an employer under 20 employees ... missing your Initial Enrollment Period can trigger the 10%-per-year penalty': imprecise or wrong. The SEP for current-employment GHP coverage doesn't require 20+ employees; size only sets which plan pays first (minor, per key).

The question about whether the plan will 'carve out' benefits for Medicare-eligible employees who aren't enrolled suggests a 20+ employer may do this to active employees, but Medicare Secondary Payer rules generally forbid it (judged from my own knowledge; harmless as a question).

reasons: Both answers open by rejecting the coworker's premise ('Don't enroll in Part B this month'). Both give the correct $202.90/month (about $2,435 a year) premium, the 8-month SEP and the HSA warning with 6-month Part A backdating. Both miss the IEP-end exception and the Medigap open-enrollment clock. A is tighter and includes the 2-month Part D window at retirement, which B lacks. B adds several correct, actionable specifics: the November 1 start if enrolled now, the 2024-MAGI IRMAA thresholds of $109,000 single and $218,000 joint, the $283 deductible, CMS-1763 for undoing an active enrollment, an explicit 'not retiree or COBRA' check with HR, the GEP fallback, and SHIP. Both slip slightly by tying the SEP to the 20-employee line, and B says it a little more explicitly. B's broader correct guidance outweighs its extra length, but only slightly.
